title: The Midnight Museum Mysteries
story: The Moon Key is missing. The museum clock has stopped. Pip borrowed the key to repair the clock; he did not intend to steal it.

tasks.title: Security Camera Check
tasks.instruction: Choose TRUE or FALSE from the *fixed* security-hall scene. Do not generate a new scene per question.

questions.prompt: There are two doors in the hall.
questions.explanation: Two doors are visible.

questions.prompt: The clock is under the desk.
questions.explanation: The clock is above the desk.

questions.prompt: There is a red bag next to the chair.
questions.explanation: The red bag is next to the chair.

questions.prompt: There are three paintings on the wall.
questions.explanation: Exactly three pictures are on the wall.

questions.prompt: The lamp is green.
questions.explanation: The lamp is yellow.

questions.prompt: There is a ticket under the bench.
questions.explanation: A ticket is under the bench.

questions.prompt: The guard has got a blue hat.
questions.explanation: The guard has a blue hat.

questions.prompt: The window is open.
questions.explanation: The window is closed.

questions.prompt: There are four keys on the desk.
questions.explanation: There are two keys on the desk.

questions.prompt: The plant is next to the stairs.
questions.explanation: The plant is near the stairs.

tasks.title: Magic Flashlight
tasks.instruction: Reveal the scene with a circular flashlight mask; students identify the object in each instruction. Hide each found item in the inventory.

questions.prompt: Find the red ticket.
Find the blue hat.
Find the yellow torch.
Find the green backpack.
Find the silver key.
Find the brown book.
Find the white glove.
Find the purple umbrella.
Find the black camera.
Find the orange ball.

tasks.title: The Ticket Machine
tasks.instruction: Show exactly 10 visitors with stable visible attributes. Display one clue at a time; click correct portrait. Use portraits as illustration cards, not random generated models.

questions.prompt: The boy has got a red cap.
The girl is wearing a green dress.
The man has got a black hat.
The woman is holding a yellow bag.
The boy has got blue shoes.
The girl is wearing a purple jacket.
The man has got glasses.
The woman is holding a red umbrella.
The boy is wearing an orange T-shirt.
The girl has got a pink scarf.

stations.name: Dinosaur Gallery
stations.focus: body parts; have got; can; present continuous

tasks.title: Build the Dinosaur
tasks.instruction: Use 10 separate bones and 10 fixed target zones. Add accessible click-to-select + click-to-place fallback; place parts in order.

questions.prompt: Put the head above the neck.
Put the neck above the body.
Put the body in the middle.
Put the tail behind the body.
Put the left arm on the left.
Put the right arm on the right.
Put the left leg under the body.
Put the right leg under the body.
Put the left foot under the left leg.
Put the right foot under the right leg.

tasks.title: Who Am I?
tasks.instruction: Show T-Rex, Triceratops and Brachiosaurus large on the screen at the same time. Click the dinosaur described.

questions.prompt: I have got two short arms.
I have got three horns.
I have got a very long neck.
I have got a big head shield.
I have got sharp teeth.
I have got a long neck and a small head.
I can run on two legs.
I have got a horn on my nose.
I can eat leaves from tall trees.
I am big and I eat meat.

tasks.title: The Moving Dinosaurs
tasks.instruction: Find each unique colour/action dinosaur from a set of 10 labelled, visually distinct character cards; gentle CSS motions are enough.

questions.prompt: The red dinosaur is running.
The green dinosaur is drinking water.
The blue dinosaur is sleeping.
The yellow dinosaur is eating leaves.
The orange dinosaur is jumping.
The purple dinosaur is hiding behind a rock.
The little dinosaur is playing with a ball.
The big dinosaur is walking slowly.
The baby dinosaur is sitting in a nest.
The brown dinosaur is looking at a bird.

stations.name: The Living Paintings
stations.focus: prepositions; descriptions; have got; there is/are

tasks.title: Repair the Paintings
tasks.instruction: Split ten placements across two pictures: first 5 village, next 5 castle. Each target slot must exist and be shown in exactly one place.

questions.prompt: Put the sun above the house.
Put the blue bird in the tree.
Put the cat under the bench.
Put two flowers in front of the house.
Put the boat on the lake.
Put the moon above the castle.
Put the owl on the castle roof.
Put a red flag on the tower.
Put three stars in the sky.
Put the little dragon behind the castle.

tasks.title: The Talking Portraits
tasks.instruction: Native speaker reads without text first; on Replay reveal English subtitle. Five portraits, each matched twice.

questions.prompt: I have got a gold crown.
I am sitting on a throne.
I am wearing a red hat.
I have got a paintbrush.
I have got a black eye patch.
I have got a treasure chest.
I am wearing glasses.
I am holding a blue bottle.
I am wearing a green dress.
I have got a white cat.

tasks.title: The Changing Picture
tasks.instruction: Two pairs, five differences per pair, 10 total. PNGs are programmatically composited from identical bases. Click target hotspot and say an English sentence.

questions.prompt: The bird is blue in picture B.
There are two apples in picture B.
The door is open in picture B.
The flowers are yellow in picture B.
The cat is under the table in picture B.
The flag is green in picture B.
There are two stars in picture B.
The dragon is behind the castle in picture B.
The left window is dark in picture B.
The boat is not on the lake in picture B.

stations.name: Egyptian Chamber
stations.focus: word order; vocabulary; clothes; prepositions; imperatives

tasks.title: Decode the Hieroglyphs
tasks.instruction: Ten sentences; replace one word with a pictogram. Choices must contain 1 correct + 2 plausible incorrect terms. Children read complete sentence after choosing.

questions.prompt: The [SUN] is yellow.
The [CAT] is sleeping.
The [SNAKE] is long.
The [BOAT] is on the river.
The [MOON] is white.
The [BIRD] can fly.
The king has got a [CROWN].
The [STAR] is blue.
The [EYE] is big.
The [KEY] is small.

tasks.title: Dress the Mummy
tasks.instruction: Place 10 wearables or handheld props on the mummy. Step 9 is a removal and must reverse the hat state.

questions.prompt: Put a blue hat on the mummy.
Put a red scarf around its neck.
Give the mummy a green bag.
Put two gold bracelets on its arms.
Put purple shoes on its feet.
Put a silver ring on its hand.
Put a white belt around its waist.
Give the mummy a small book.
Take off the blue hat.
Put a golden crown on its head.

tasks.title: Escape the Pyramid
tasks.instruction: Show a ten-checkpoint route with arrow controls. Each instruction consumes one checkpoint and triggers a visual animation; keyboard arrows work too.

questions.prompt: Go straight to the first door.
Turn left at the cat statue.
Go right at the big vase.
Walk past the green snake.
Stop next to the golden box.
Go straight to the blue door.
Turn right at the two torches.
Go left at the river.
Walk over the bridge.
Open the door with the moon.

tasks.title: What Has Disappeared?
tasks.instruction: Display ten distinct cards for 12–15 seconds; hide the cover for each fast round. One item disappears per round; preserve other nine in fixed positions. Give four answer options if pupils struggle.

questions.prompt: The yellow hat is missing.
The blue cup is missing.
The silver coin is missing.
The red star is missing.
The golden bell is missing.
The purple book is missing.
The white glove is missing.
The green scarf is missing.
The red apple is missing.
The small spoon is missing.

tasks.title: Whose Is It?
tasks.instruction: Ten owners on left / ten possessions right. Put only one characteristic item per owner; auto snap correct matches.

questions.prompt: The artist has got a paintbrush.
The explorer has got a map.
The king has got a crown.
The scientist has got a blue bottle.
The pirate has got a compass.
The guard has got a torch.
The cook has got a spoon.
The girl has got a pink ribbon.
The boy has got a toy dinosaur.
The queen has got a golden necklace.

tasks.title: The Detective Evidence Board
tasks.instruction: Show pinned evidence pictures 1–5; answers are directly grounded in the inventory and fixed scene.

questions.prompt: The footprints are small.
questions.explanation: The prints are tiny.

questions.prompt: The footprints are on the ceiling.
questions.explanation: The prints are on the floor.

questions.prompt: There is grey fur on the floor.
questions.explanation: Grey fur was found in Gallery 2.

questions.prompt: The fur is pink.
questions.explanation: The fur is grey.

questions.prompt: There is a long tail in the photo.
questions.explanation: The picture showed a long tail.

questions.prompt: The Moon Key is made of wood.
questions.explanation: The Moon Key is golden.

questions.prompt: There is gold dust on the stairs.
questions.explanation: Gold dust was found near the chamber stairs.

questions.prompt: The note says, “I want to help.”
questions.explanation: These are the exact words.

questions.prompt: The museum window is broken.
questions.explanation: The window is closed and unbroken.

questions.prompt: The clock is working.
questions.explanation: The clock is still stopped.

stations.name: The Clock Tower
stations.focus: numbers; missing words; grammar revision; deduction

tasks.title: Fix the Giant Clock
tasks.instruction: A full 12-hour clock: 10 and 11 are already fixed and the remaining ten positions are empty. Number tokens are draggable.

questions.prompt: Put twelve at the top.
Put six at the bottom.
Put three on the right.
Put nine on the left.
Put one after twelve.
Put two after one.
Put four after three.
Put five after four.
Put seven after six.
Put eight after seven.

tasks.title: Repair the Broken Sentences
tasks.instruction: One short sentence with two answer buttons; each right answer spins a gear.

questions.prompt: There ___ a key in the box.
There ___ three doors in the hall.
The cat is ___ the table.
The dinosaur ___ got a long tail.
The paintings ___ moving.
The mummy is ___ a hat.
The owl ___ fly.
The mouse is ___ the clock.
___ there two lamps?
The clock ___ working.

tasks.title: Who Took the Moon Key?
tasks.instruction: Show suspects Owl, Cat, Bat, Fox, Mouse plus accumulated evidence. Present true/false characteristics then click mouse.

questions.prompt: The mystery animal is small.
questions.explanation: Small pawprints point to a small animal.

questions.prompt: It has got grey fur.
questions.explanation: Grey fur.

questions.prompt: It has got a long tail.
questions.explanation: Long tail.

questions.prompt: It has got wings.
questions.explanation: Pip has no wings.

questions.prompt: It can fly.
questions.explanation: Pip cannot fly.

questions.prompt: It has got big round ears.
questions.explanation: Mouse ears.

questions.prompt: It is wearing a gold crown.
questions.explanation: Pip has brass goggles, not a crown.

questions.prompt: It is hiding in the clock.
questions.explanation: Pip is inside the clock mechanism.

questions.prompt: It has got the Moon Key.
questions.explanation: Pip is holding the key.

questions.prompt: It wants to help.
questions.explanation: The message says so.

settings.timerPolicy: soft countdown; optional; auto-prompt to switch to quick mode at <60s
